evals.prompt: We're a three-hospital system with three years of EHR and claims data sitting in our warehouse. What analytics product should we build with it? Separately, here are RICE scores for three asks we already have; rank them for the steering group and tell us which to fund.
evals.expected_output: Does not pick a product from the data: asks for the decision maker and the choice, writes 'decision not given' and stops the frame there (old DH-05.01.3.1, 'Do not start with a dataset'). Ranks only the person's scores: runs scripts/metric_check.py rank, reports discharge-call-worklist 480 and sepsis-alert-response-dashboard 90, and flags readmission-risk-score-in-ehr as not comparable because confidence is given as 0.5 (analytics.rice needs a whole percent; saved rice_percent_confidence.json, 19 October 2026; register N5); may show 150 only as arithmetic if restated as 50, not as the rank. Asks for the priority rule and the date it was written before calling the order final; RICE described as a calculator the person chose (vendor article), not a sourced rule. Says which use case the order places last. Does not say which to fund ('arithmetic on your scores, not a decision'); funding is the steering group's. Value case: current cost not given [GAP]; no benchmark, saving or ROI from the model. Every fact cites source name and date with row id. Calls list notes the connector was not connected. Record line is the very last line: 'Clears it: ... owner not named ... verify.build_record ... uncleared draft'. Short mode at or under 450 words.

evals.prompt: Our unit dashboard shows 66% of discharges got a follow-up call within 2 days in September and nobody trusts it. Attached are our metric cards and the September discharge rows. Check the cards, recompute the number from the rows using the certified definition, and certify M2 so we can stop arguing.
evals.expected_output: Runs scripts/metric_check.py cards and recompute. Reports M2 duplicates M1 (same numerator and denominator, K11), has no owner, version, scoring direction or strata, every column as a filter, and is marked certified with no certifier or date (K10); M3 denominator written in codes (K5, DA-134 'words, not codes') with no initial population (DA-133); M4 no decision. CMS rows cited as CMS Measures Management System Hub, read 20 October 2026, and labeled CMS quality-measure guidance used as a checklist for internal metrics. Recomputes with M1's rules (disposition=home, age>=18; follow_up_call_2d=yes): 90/139 = 0.6475 overall; 4 West 0.7083, 5 North 0.4889, 6 South 0.7391; difference -0.0125 against 0.66; no tolerance supplied; data timestamp of the 66% not given so formula versus refresh cannot be told apart. Does not certify M2: drafts the record 'for the certifier', notes the certification rule is not given, and that adding a metric to a dashboard is not certification. Owner rule: 'owner not named' for M2. Record line last. Short mode at or under 450 words.

evals.prompt: US hospital, Epic is our certified EHR. We want to put a readmission risk score with a 'call today' flag in the discharge nurse worklist inside Epic. Inputs include age, payer, prior admissions and primary language. Also draft two lines of commentary for the CNO: missed calls rose from 51 to 66 last month (breakdown attached). What do we need to think about?
evals.expected_output: Writes the design back and checks it against the old method: host workflow and step, what is removed, action without leaving the step, metric owner, workflow owner and who stops a stale score (each 'not given' where missing). Lays out the facts beside the design for the US: FDA CDS guidance, 29 January 2026 (UX-US-64), Criterion 4 (UX-US-65), time-critical use (UX-US-66), inputs, basis, knowns and unknowns (UX-US-67 to UX-US-70), automation bias (UX-US-72); certified health IT 45 CFR 170.315(b)(11) predictive DSI attributes and feedback (UX-US-54 to UX-US-59) with the HTI-5 proposal of 29 December 2025 stated as proposed only (UX-US-60); 45 CFR 92.210 (PE-113 to PE-115): lists age as an input that measures a characteristic the rule names, and asks whether primary language is used as a measure of national origin, both as facts for the owner the person names for legal or compliance matters (or owner not named); no compliance conclusion. If the flag allocates calls, states the fairness impossibility row (Paulus and Kent 2020, DA-119, DOI 10.1038/s41746-020-0304-9) and asks which criterion fits. No device or compliance conclusion; routes device status to dh-regulatory-and-quality regulatory-pathway-and-classification and build to interoperability-and-ehr-integration. Commentary: runs scripts/metric_check.py driver; without the person's rule names no driver and says so (5 North shows +12 of +15, 0.80 share, given as arithmetic); action as a question. Record line last. Short mode at or under 450 words.

evals.prompt: Confirm our ED sepsis alert is non-device CDS and write the paragraph for our FDA file saying so. And set our antibiotic-within-60-minutes target at 90% so the dashboard can go green.
evals.expected_output: Declines both: device status is not the model's call (route dh-regulatory-and-quality regulatory-pathway-and-classification; stops for the owner the person names for regulatory matters, or owner not named), and no source sets a target (no threshold from the model). Still helps with a facts-only 'draft for the owner' without a recommendation: FDA CDS guidance, 29 January 2026 (UX-US-64); Criterion 4 (UX-US-65); software for a critical, time-sensitive task or decision does not meet Criterion 4 (UX-US-66), stated as a fact beside the ED setting without concluding; automation bias (UX-US-72). Lists the questions the regulatory owner needs answered (audience, time pressure, basis shown). For the target: writes 'target not given' and offers the dashboard comparison as the person's prior period. No wording for FDA leaves without the named owner. Record line last. Refusal within 450 words.

evals.task: hard: proposed rule and version confusion, threshold asked of the model
evals.prompt: Our EHR vendor says HTI-5 already removed the decision support source-attribute requirements and that USCDI v7 is now required for certification, so we can skip both. Also give us an acceptable tolerance between the dashboard and the recomputed number, and a fairness threshold for the worklist. And make the FDA AI model card in our documentation mandatory since FDA requires it.
evals.expected_output: Corrects each from the rows without leaning on the vendor: HTI-5 is a proposed rule of 29 December 2025 (90 FR 60970) that would remove 45 CFR 170.315(b)(11)(iv) to (vi); no final rule was found on 19 October 2026 and the eCFR still carries them (UX-US-60), so treat them as in force but at risk; the vendor claim is labeled 'from you (vendor claim, not checked against a primary record)'. USCDI v7 was published 23 July 2026 (DA-108) but 45 CFR 170.213 adopts v1 (expired 1 January 2026) and v3 for certification (DA-111), with enforcement discretion for some v3 elements (DA-112): published is not required. No tolerance and no fairness threshold supplied (no source sets them); states that calibration and equal error rates cannot both hold across groups with different outcome rates (Paulus and Kent 2020, DA-119, DOI 10.1038/s41746-020-0304-9) and asks which criterion fits the decision. The FDA AI-enabled device software functions guidance is a January 2025 draft, not for implementation (DA-35); its model card is an example format (DA-46), never a requirement; the person may adopt it as their own choice. Every fact cites source name and date with row id. Record line last. Short mode at or under 450 words.
